articulation.label: information
articulation.alt: information: /ɪ/ → /n/ → /f/ → /ɚ/ → /m/ → /eɪ/ → /ʃ/ → /ə/ → /n/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/n/: Tip at the ridge; air goes through the nose.
/f/: Upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip.
/m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
/ɪ/: Raise the front tongue; narrow the jaw gap.
/ʃ/: Tongue blade just behind the ridge; air flows.
/ə/: Relax the tongue in the center.
/n/: Tip at the ridge; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Your A1 checkpoint
sections: Try the five tasks before opening the models. A partner may speak slowly or repeat. Listen to the dictation and write what you hear.
Ask where a library is. Follow or give two simple directions.
Ask for a ticket and check its destination and time.
Give the name on a hotel reservation and ask about the room.
Write a short message with a meeting place and time.

Report one simple problem and ask for help.
Review words: office, battery, elevator, warning, platform. Cover the list; recall meanings and use two in your own sentences.
cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 120 - Review & Check - 01
cards.answer:
Dictation: Across the road.
1: For example: Turn right. It is near the park.
2: For example: A single ticket to Oak Town, please. What time does the train leave?
3: For example: I have a reservation under Lee. Which floor is the room on?
4: For example: Meet me at the station at two.
5: For example: The lamp doesn’t work. Can you help me, please?
For each task, note: I can do it; I can do it with repetition; I need more practice. Repeat difficult tasks another day with new details. Clear meaning matters more than a perfect accent.
